back2basics.text: External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) are loans raised by Indian entities from foreign sources. Foreign Currency Convertible Bonds (FCCBs) are bonds issued in foreign currency that can be converted into equity shares. Rupee Denominated Bonds (RDBs) are bonds issued outside India but denominated in Indian Rupees. These instruments are important for raising foreign capital and affect the country's external debt and currency stability.

back2basics.text: The right to privacy is a fundamental right recognized by the Supreme Court, protecting individuals' personal information. Press freedom is also constitutionally guaranteed, allowing journalists to operate independently. Laws like the DPDP Act must balance protecting personal data with ensuring that journalistic activities are not hindered.

2026-10-30-am-4607810f22.deck: IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated on October 28, 2026, that the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act does not infringe on press freedom, affirming constitutional guarantees for journalistic independence. This clarification is crucial amid concerns from news publishers about the law's impact on investigative journalism and data handling.

back2basics.text: The IIP measures the short-term changes in the volume of production of a basket of industrial products during a given period relative to a base year. It covers key sectors like mining, manufacturing, electricity, and water supply. The base year is periodically revised to reflect current industrial structures and production patterns, ensuring the index remains relevant and accurate for economic analysis and policy-making.

back2basics.text: The NHRC is a statutory body established to protect and promote human rights in India. It can take suo motu cognizance of violations, issue notices to authorities, and recommend actions to ensure accountability. It acts as a watchdog over law enforcement agencies to prevent abuse and uphold dignity and rights of individuals.

2026-10-30-am-86f95ea671.deck: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has taken suo motu cognizance of media reports that Kolkata police paraded three persons in a semi-nude condition with ropes tied around their waists. This raises serious human rights concerns and highlights issues of police accountability and dignity of arrested persons, important for understanding constitutional bodies and human rights protection.

back2basics.concept: Digital arrest scams and financial due diligence
back2basics.text: Digital arrest scams are cyber frauds where criminals impersonate police or government officials via phone calls to extort money. Financial institutions have a due diligence responsibility to monitor and prevent suspicious transactions to protect customers. Regulatory frameworks like Know Your Customer (KYC) guidelines help banks verify identities and detect fraud, ensuring financial stability and consumer protection.

2026-10-30-am-b527fe462f.deck: The Supreme Court on October 29, 2026, urged the Reserve Bank of India to mandate financial institutions to compensate victims of digital arrest scams caused by institutional negligence. This ruling highlights judicial efforts to curb cyber fraud and protect citizens’ digital rights, relevant for both Prelims and Mains.

back2basics.text: A witness protection scheme is a legal framework designed to safeguard witnesses who may face threats or intimidation for their testimony in criminal cases. It typically includes threat assessment, protective measures, dedicated authorities, and funds to ensure witness safety, thereby strengthening the criminal justice system by encouraging truthful testimony without fear.

back2basics.concept: Banking Regulation Act and RBI's supervisory role
back2basics.text: The Banking Regulation Act, 1949, empowers the Reserve Bank of India to regulate banking companies including cooperative banks. Under this Act, RBI can issue directions to banks to ensure their sound functioning and protect depositors' interests. Sections 35A and 56 allow RBI to impose restrictions or conditions on cooperative banks when their financial position or management raises concerns. This regulatory oversight helps maintain financial stability and public confidence in the banking system.

2026-10-30-am-f9733158e2.deck: The Reserve Bank of India has extended its directions under Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, for three cooperative banks until January 30, 2027. This extension reflects RBI's ongoing regulatory oversight to ensure public interest and financial stability in the cooperative banking sector.

back2basics.text: The Employees’ State Insurance (ESI) Scheme is a social security and health insurance scheme for Indian workers. It provides medical care and cash benefits to insured persons and their families in case of sickness, maternity, disability, or death due to employment injury. The scheme is implemented by the Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) under the Ministry of Labour & Employment. Disputes can arise over contributions or compliance, which the amnesty scheme aims to resolve amicably.

2026-10-30-am-f9ec4b14b4.deck: The Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) has extended the New Amnesty Scheme 2025 by three months till December 31, 2026, allowing more time for employers and insured persons to resolve pending disputes. This extension is important for UPSC aspirants as it relates to social security and labour welfare policies under the erstwhile ESI Act.

Consider the following statements about the ESIC New Amnesty Scheme 2025:

2. Court cases filed up to December 31, 2026, are eligible under the scheme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because only court cases filed up to March 31, 2025, are eligible under the scheme, not those filed up to December 31, 2026.

body.label: One-time dispute resolution
body.text: The scheme is a one-time initiative to reduce the backlog of court cases related to the erstwhile ESI Act by promoting out-of-court settlements between employers and ESIC.

body.label: Settlement terms
body.text: Employers can settle ad-hoc assessments by paying actual contributions and interest without damages, and cases where dues are paid can be withdrawn by paying 10% of disputed damages.

body.label: Eligibility criteria
body.text: Court cases filed up to March 31, 2025, are eligible for settlement under this scheme.

sections.heading: What is the ESIC New Amnesty Scheme 2025?

body.label: Stakeholder representations
body.text: The extension followed a review of representations from various stakeholders seeking more time to resolve pending cases.

body.label: Promoting compliance
body.text: The extension supports ESIC’s commitment to reducing litigation and promoting voluntary compliance among employers and insured persons.

body.label: Ease of doing business
body.text: The scheme aligns with the government’s broader goal of enhancing ease of doing business while protecting the rights of insured persons.

sections.heading: Why was the scheme extended till December 31, 2026?

body.label: Reduced financial burden
body.text: Employers can avoid paying damages on ad-hoc assessments and settle dues by paying actual contributions and interest.

body.label: Withdrawal of cases
body.text: Cases filed by ESIC for non-submission of records or delayed payments, which were later complied with, can be withdrawn with court permission.

body.label: Additional time
body.text: The extension gives eligible employers and insured persons more time to avail the benefits of the scheme until December 31, 2026.
